body:
I don't think this is the correct usage for this. The argument is the record name and it should not have brackets.

Try:

``` erb
<%= form_for :foos, url: root_path do |f| %>
  <% @foos.each do |foo| %>
    <%= f.fields_for "foo", foo, index: nil do |f2| %>
      <%= f2.fields_for :bars do |b| %>
        <%= f2.text_field :id %>
        <%= b.text_field :id %>
      <% end %>
    <% end %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

In this case we'll got "foos[foo][][id]" and "foos[foo][bars][id]" -> "expected Hash (got Array) for param `foo'" error.
So it also doesn't work.

Actually my first testcase worked fine: 'foo[]' works for object creation, but fails for updates (i. e. if object has id).
I've updated the [test repo](https://github.com/ojab/nested_fail/commits/master) with all `foo[] || foo, index: nil` & `Foo.new || Foo.create` combinations (one per commit), field names and results are included in commit messages.

Basically there is a mismatch between [form_for](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/tags/base.rb#L14) and [fields_for](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_helper.rb#L1250) tag naming.
It can be fixed with something like [this](https://github.com/ojab/rails/commit/20b955c5be5ffac3436135939d6ec6b344cc79a7). Could you please point me how it should be implemented properly? I can clearly see that second part is too ugly.
@ojab where you able to fix this? Been trying to do something similar and ran into the same issue
@rafaelfranca did you ever get around to checking out @ojab's suggestion?

@ojab to generate what you've hard coded using rails you should use `accept_nested_attributes_for`, check this link as an example http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2212622/accepts-nested-attributes-for-with-has-many-through-options

issue.title: Handle nested fields_for by adding indexes to record_name
